analysis.title: Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN): Robust expense discipline and growth in newer products, offset by weaker near-term revenue outlook
key_insights: COIN reported 3Q26 EPS of $2.51 (reported), above GSe/Visible Alpha consensus of +$1.88/-$0.04. Excluding one-timers, GS pegs core EPS at $0.71 vs GSe/consensus of $0.54/$0.48, driven by core operating expenses (ex. SBC) 5% lower than the Street.
GS expects a modestly negative stock reaction to the print because of the weaker outlook, despite the quarterly beat.

Management guided 4Q/FY26 adj. operating expenses down by $100mn at the midpoint, to $1.007bn-1.157bn for 4Q26 and $4.15bn-4.3bn for FY26. This is the second FY26 opex guide-down this year, a cumulative $200mn (5%) reduction YTD.

Prediction markets passed ~$200mn annualized revenue in 3Q26 (from ~$100mn in 2Q26, compounding 82% quarterly since 1Q26). DAUs rose >60% QoQ and non-sports contracts were >50% of volumes, largely driven by crypto prediction markets.

COIN received a Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) license, enabling it to list event contracts as a Designated Contract Market (DCM). GS says this lets COIN earn both brokerage and exchange fees and control contract design.
3Q26 was the fifth consecutive quarter of record high-value Coinbase One (CB1) paid subscribers. CB1 customers generate 3.5x the ARPU of other COIN users, with higher retention.
Total payment volume on the Coinbase Developer Platform has compounded 160% quarterly since 4Q25. Non-US tokenized equities trading has had >$3bn of volume since launch.
Management said prediction markets have not cannibalized spot crypto trading volumes.
Transaction revenue was $590mn, in line with consensus and down 44% YoY. Retail transaction revenue was 1% above the Street and institutional was 7% below.
4Q26 quarter-to-date transaction revenue is ~$165mn, equal to ~$607mn if run-rated for the full quarter, 11% below consensus on a day-count-adjusted basis.

Subscription and services revenue was $570mn (-2% vs GSe, +1% vs consensus) and down 24% YoY. Other and staking revenue were 4% and 3% below the Street, while interest and stablecoin revenue were 7% and 3% above. 4Q26 guidance of $550-630mn has a midpoint ~5% below consensus.
Prime brokerage is expanding, with the average daily loan book balance up 74% YoY.

Adj. expenses (ex. SBC) of $921mn fell 21% YoY and were 8% below consensus. G&A and tech and dev expenses were 10% and 4% lower than consensus, offset by 9% higher transaction-related expense. The FY26 adj. expense guide is 1% below the Street, and the 4Q26 midpoint is 4% below implied Street estimates. Management also guided 4Q26 transaction expenses to mid-teens as a % of net revenue and SBC to ~$240mn.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E total revenue by 4%/8%/5% and adj. expenses by 2%/3%/1%. Adj. pre-tax margins (ex. SBC) fall by 2.2pp/3.9pp/2.6pp. Adj. EPS falls by 3%/18%/10%.
GS lowers its target P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS by 3.0x to 30.0x, cutting the 12-month price target 14% to $210 from $244. Rating stays Buy, with 30.8% upside from $160.59.

GS stays constructive on COIN's long-term growth across crypto trading and prediction markets, citing scale, profitability and distribution relative to competitors in a tepid crypto trading environment.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut its price target 14% from $244 after weaker 4Q26 revenue guidance and lower estimates, and lowered its target P/E to 30.0x. It keeps the Buy on expense discipline and growth in prediction markets, Coinbase One and stablecoin payments.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 EPS $2.51 reported, vs GSe/Visible Alpha consensus of +$1.88/-$0.04. Core EPS ex-one-timers is $0.71 (GS estimate), vs GSe $0.54 and consensus $0.48. Adjustments cover data theft recovery, restructuring expense, gains and losses on crypto assets (including a $210mn loss on crypto assets held for investment and strategic investments), tax normalization and SBC.
3Q26 transaction revenue $590mn reported, in line with consensus, down 44% YoY. 3Q26 subscription and services revenue $570mn reported, -2% vs GSe and +1% vs consensus, down 24% YoY.

4Q26 guidance: QTD transaction revenue ~$165mn (~$607mn run-rated, 11% below consensus), subscription and services revenue $550-630mn (midpoint ~5% below consensus), adj. expenses $1.007bn-1.157bn, transaction expenses mid-teens % of net revenue, SBC ~$240mn.
FY26 adj. expense guide $4.15bn-4.30bn, ~$100mn lower at the midpoint and 1% below the Street.
crypto_views: COIN's trading environment is described as persistently tepid, but the company has more scale, profitability and distribution than its competitors.

Prediction markets are running at ~$200mn annualized revenue and non-sports contracts are >50% of volume, largely crypto prediction markets. Management reports no cannibalization of spot crypto trading volumes.
Non-US tokenized equities trading has had >$3bn of volume since launch.
Stablecoin payments on the Coinbase Developer Platform have compounded 160% quarterly since 4Q25. Interest and stablecoin revenue ran 7% above GSe and 3% above consensus in 3Q26.
GS lists crypto deregulatory reform falling short and crypto market cap trending down over time as downside risks.
risk_factors: Product evolution outside of trading takes longer than expected.
Crypto market cap trends down over time.
Sports prediction contracts carry more legal challenge risk than non-sports contracts.

tension_points.bull_case: Expense discipline (a cumulative $200mn, or 5%, FY26 opex guide-down YTD) and growth in newer products support the long-term case. Prediction markets reached ~$200mn annualized, record Coinbase One subscribers, rising stablecoin payments, and no cannibalization of spot volumes. GS keeps a Buy and a $210 target.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q26 QTD transaction revenue of ~$165mn is 11% below the Street when day-count adjusted. Subscription and services guidance has a midpoint ~5% below consensus. GS cuts 2027E revenue by 8% and 2027E EPS by 18%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS lists its downside risks as insufficient crypto deregulatory reform, slower product evolution outside trading, crypto market cap trending down over time, and pricing pressure on margins.
